# Step 2.234, the second fix round (the brief, written by the eighteenth lead on 2026-11-27)

The lead who runs it gives it its usual head: the shared rules file, the lane folder `.local/lanes/2.234` (branch `lane/2.234-wrong-tries`, newest c27f7706), effort high, AT MOST 80 COMMANDS, decision numbers T-511 and T-512, migration 0034 if the change to `sign_in.codes` needs one (the lane's 0033 may be edited instead while it has not landed: prefer that), a report of at most 10 lines.

## What the confirming look (the strongest model, 2026-11-27) found

1. **High (T-68), proved on both adapters:** after a stranger's reset ask and wrong codes, an address whose owner is mid-reset on a known device answers `code-wrong` without end, then `code-expired` at the OWNER's expiry; an address with no account answers `code-wrong` x4 then `too-many-attempts`. Causes: attempts never run out for a non-owner (`local-sign-in.ts:359-372`, `take-code-attempt.ts:17-27`); the held ask writes nothing (`local-sign-in.ts:244-247`, `supabase-sign-in.ts:263-274`).
2. **High (T-68, by time and calls), real adapter:** the held path (`supabase-sign-in.ts:262-274`) returns before `auth.generateCode`, `store.accounts.accountExists` and `putCode`, so it answers one Supabase round trip sooner than a reset for an address without an account.
3. Low: the sweep of old limit rows (`guess-counts.ts:62-71`, `count-code-request.ts:30-34`) is safe only while every caller passes the same `windowMinutes`; a `lockMinutes` longer than the window would let it delete the guesses behind a live lock.
4. Low: `reviewed-definers.ts:53`'s reason for `erase_account` says "(0012)" and names no sign-in rows.

## The lead's decisions (build them on BOTH adapters; items in order, item 1 first)

1. **T-511:** an unknown device's held ask gets ITS OWN code-less waiting entry beside the known device's: its own 5 attempts and its own 10 minutes from its own ask; `sign_in.codes` is keyed by address plus known-device-or-none; each verifier reads and spends only its own entry. So a stranger sees exactly what they would see for an address with no account. On the real adapter's held path, make the same calls a no-account reset makes (`generateCode('recovery', <a made-up address>)`, `accountExists(token())`, `putCode` of the stranger's entry), so time and calls match.
2. Add an address mid-reset on a known device to both `*-identical` tests (words, status, cookies, the adapter's calls), and the look's exact attack as a test on both adapters. Break each by hand once and see it fail.
3. **T-512:** the sweep deletes only rows older than the longer of the window and the lock, whatever a caller passes; a test with a lock longer than the window.
4. Correct `erase_account`'s reason in `reviewed-definers.ts`.
5. `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, the sign-in vitest folders, the database sign-in/erase tests, `npm run test:real-postgres`, `node scripts/run-web-browser-tests.mjs known-device-test`; commit; at most 12 lines in the note.

Left, written in the note only: while a known device's code waits, the owner asking from a NEW phone gets no mail for up to 10 minutes (it is an unknown device); a stranger's 5 asks an hour for an address also use the known device's asks (T-509).
